raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

The Rust frontend accepted several malformed structured-output requests that the Python frontend rejects at request time. This brings the two frontends into parity so invalid requests fail fast with a `400` instead of being forwarded to engine-core as ambiguous params or surfacing later as opaque generation failures.

Four parity fixes, each mirroring the corresponding Python validation:

1. **Mutual exclusivity** of constraints in the `structured_outputs` blob — exactly one of `json`/`regex`/`choice`/`grammar`/`json_object`/`structural_tag`. Mirrors `StructuredOutputsParams.__post_init__` (`vllm/sampling_params.py:90-111`).
2. **Null `json_schema`** — `response_format: {type: json_schema, json_schema: {schema: null}}` is now rejected. Python lowers a null schema to `json=None`, which then fails the "must use one constraint" check.
3. **`structural_tag` shape** — a tag matching neither the legacy (`structures`/`triggers`) nor current (`format`) shape is rejected at request time. Mirrors `validate_structural_tag_response_format` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py:167-197`).
4. **Structured outputs + named tool** — combining structured outputs with a specific `tool_choice` function is rejected. Mirrors `chat_completion/protocol.py:800-809`.

Each fix references the Python source it mirrors and adds regression tests (property-based via `proptest`, plus example-based cases).

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for structured-output / structural_tag / mutual-exclusivity validation in the Rust frontend — no existing PR addresses these request-validation gaps.

## Testing

```
cargo clippy -p vllm-server          # clean, no warnings
cargo fmt -p vllm-server
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib structured_outputs                 # 10 passed
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib chat_completions::convert::tests   # 30 passed
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib                                    # full lib suite passes
```

Note: `tls_tests::tls_handshake_timeout_drops_silent_client` is timing-sensitive and flaked once locally on macOS (passes on re-run; unrelated to these changes, which do not touch TLS/networking).

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to help author these changes. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the structural_tag payload, not just its keys**

With this shortcut, any object containing `format` (and any legacy object with array-valued `structures`/`triggers`) is accepted, including payloads such as `{"type":"structural_tag","format":{}}` that the Python function cited by this change rejects after calling the xgrammar structural-tag validator. Those malformed current-shape tags are still forwarded to engine-core and can surface as generation failures instead of the intended 400 request error, so the Rust validation is not actually in parity for the main `format` shape.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

@@ -48,17 +48,79 @@ pub enum ResponseFormat {
     },
 }
 
+/// Validate that exactly one structured-output constraint field is set.
+///
+/// Mirrors the mutual-exclusivity check in Python's
+/// `StructuredOutputsParams.__post_init__`:
+/// <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f22d6e026/vllm/sampling_params.py#L90-L111>
+fn validate_single_constraint(params: &StructuredOutputsParams) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
+    let count = [
+        params.json.is_some(),
+        params.regex.is_some(),
+        params.choice.is_some(),
+        params.grammar.is_some(),
+        params.json_object.is_some(),
+        params.structural_tag.is_some(),
+    ]
+    .into_iter()
+    .filter(|set| *set)
+    .count();
+    match count {
+        1 => Ok(()),
+        0 => Err(ApiError::invalid_request(
+            "You must use one kind of structured outputs constraint but none \
+             are specified",
+            Some("structured_outputs"),
+        )),
+        _ => Err(ApiError::invalid_request(
+            "You can only use one kind of structured outputs constraint but \
+             multiple are specified",
+            Some("structured_outputs"),
+        )),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Validate that a `structural_tag` payload matches one of the two shapes vLLM
+/// accepts, mirroring Python's `AnyStructuralTagResponseFormat`:
+///
+/// - legacy: `structures` (array) and `triggers` (array)
+/// - current: `format`
+///
+/// Python validates the shape at request time so malformed tags are rejected
+/// as bad requests rather than surfacing later as opaque generation failures:
+/// <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f22d6e026/vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py#L167-L197>
+fn validate_structural_tag_shape(extra: &serde_json::Map<String, Value>) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
+    let invalid = || {
+        ApiError::invalid_request(
+            "Invalid response_format structural_tag specification",
+            Some("response_format"),
+        )
+    };
+
+    if extra.contains_key("format") {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let legacy_shaped = extra.get("structures").is_some_and(Value::is_array)
+        && extra.get("triggers").is_some_and(Value::is_array);

The current-shape branch now deserializes the tag into the typed `xgrammar_structural_tag::StructuralTag` instead of just checking for a `format` key, so a malformed payload like `{"type":"structural_tag","format":{}}` (or an unknown `format.type`) is rejected as a 400 rather than forwarded to engine-core — mirroring Python's `validate_structural_tag_payload` xgrammar check. A valid typed `format` (e.g. `{"type":"any_text"}`) still passes, and the legacy `structures`/`triggers` shape is unchanged. Moved the empty-`format` case into `malformed_structural_tag_rejected` and updated `well_formed_structural_tag_accepted` to use a valid typed format.

The current-shape branch now deserializes the tag into the typed `xgrammar_structural_tag::StructuralTag` instead of just checking for a `format` key, so a malformed payload like `{"type":"structural_tag","format":{}}` (or an unknown `format.type`) is rejected as a 400 rather than forwarded to engine-core — mirroring Python's `validate_structural_tag_payload` xgrammar check. A valid typed `format` (e.g. `{"type":"any_text"}`) still passes, and the legacy `structures`/`triggers` shape is unchanged. Moved the empty-`format` case into `malformed_structural_tag_rejected` and updated `well_formed_structural_tag_accepted` to use a valid typed format.

+/// Validate that exactly one structured-output constraint field is set.
+///
+/// Mirrors the mutual-exclusivity check in Python's
+/// `StructuredOutputsParams.__post_init__`:
+/// <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f22d6e026/vllm/sampling_params.py#L90-L111>
+fn validate_single_constraint(params: &StructuredOutputsParams) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
+    let count = [
+        params.json.is_some(),
+        params.regex.is_some(),
+        params.choice.is_some(),
+        params.grammar.is_some(),
+        params.json_object.is_some(),
+        params.structural_tag.is_some(),
+    ]
+    .into_iter()
+    .filter(|set| *set)
+    .count();
+    match count {
+        1 => Ok(()),
+        0 => Err(ApiError::invalid_request(

+             are specified",
+            Some("structured_outputs"),
+        )),

+             multiple are specified",

+}

+/// Validate that a `structural_tag` payload matches one of the two shapes vLLM
+/// accepts, mirroring Python's `AnyStructuralTagResponseFormat`:
+///
+/// - legacy: `structures` (array) and `triggers` (array)
+/// - current: `format`
+///
+/// Python validates the shape at request time so malformed tags are rejected
+/// as bad requests rather than surfacing later as opaque generation failures:
+/// <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f22d6e026/vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py#L167-L197>
+fn validate_structural_tag_shape(extra: &serde_json::Map<String, Value>) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
+    let invalid = || {
+        ApiError::invalid_request(
+            "Invalid response_format structural_tag specification",
+            Some("response_format"),
+        )
+    };
+
+    if extra.contains_key("format") {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let legacy_shaped = extra.get("structures").is_some_and(Value::is_array)
+        && extra.get("triggers").is_some_and(Value::is_array);
